Tried it during the free week. The UI was horrible and cluttered, which is a shame because the other art and world design is good. The rest of the game aspects are bad. Destiny should not have died for this.

By the way, the solution to "fixing Marathon" (which can't happen) is not to jam other game modes like PVE into the game. Turning the game into something else is a silent admission that your original game was bad. Marathon should've just been a PVE game from the start. It's truly a shame that the development team at Bungie has to take the fall for the blunder of the executives and Sony.

After spending 2 months watching streamers play this game, I finally decided to buy it and try it out myself. I pulled the trigger for two main reasons: the absolutely insane lore and the stunning weapon models. Even though I hadn't played a single match, I already knew about all of its issues xD, so I was prepared for the worst.
1. After barely pushing through the tutorial run and successfully exfiling, the game threw me right into that infamous UI/UX that literally everyone has been complaining about — the same one that more than a few YouTubers have used to build their careers over the past 5 months. Honestly, guys, I had ZERO issues with it. Everything is completely intuitive. Don't buy into the hate.
2. Once I figured out how to use the free deployment kit, how to buy gear from factions, and how to pick up contracts, I rushed straight into the perimeter. My first two runs ended instantly — I got blown up by some random rockets before I could even reach the first shelter. On my third attempt, I finally made it to the buildings, only for the bots to completely destroy me without a fighting chance.
3. The guns and the shooting mechanics absolutely did not disappoint. And the weapons look amazing—they aren't some glowing alien blasters that make no sense, but actual, recognizable bullet-firing guns set in a slightly futuristic world. I love that they look modular rather than just a single solid pre-drawn model. This allows for a massive variety of animations, and the developers definitely didn't skimp on them. This gunplay is the exact reason why I keep wanting to go back to the perimeter, face those annoying bots again, and finally finish that first quest to get that badass rifle as a reward. I’m a huge fan of shooting mechanics, and every single gun here has its own distinct sound, animations, and recoil.
If you love great gunplay as much as I do — highly recommended!

This game has no cohesive identity and has no idea what it wants to be. The gameplay itself is fine and gunplay feels satisfying but it is not fun, extremely confusing, and UI that is so stupid that it honestly should be required coursework for game developers on what not to do. I literally quit mid-match and refunded it realizing that it is just not fun and it is wasting my time.

Worst UI I've ever had to use. It's like the developers made navigating the game difficult and non-intuitive on purpose there is no way that is by accident. Load times are atrocious. Getting into a game has been about a five minute wait. I cant even get into another game until I acknowledge that I completed some kind of achievement from the last game. I don't even know where to go in the mess of menus to do that. And why is that even a thing? Why do I need to do that? Cant set hotkeys to items, I have to browse inventory to use an item. Why cant I just set a button for med kit? 

So right now I'm locked out of starting a game because I need to go to contracts and probably click something five or six times then read a few pages of lore or something of the like. Maybe I'll come back to it when I feel like searching through the bizarre UI and figuring out how to get another game started. Just getting into a game is a chore. This game is reminding me to much of work already. Spent about one hour playing and about 15 minutes of that is actual time spent in game. The rest is either spent trying to navigate the atrocious UI to get into a game or staring at a load screen.

One of the worst UI experiences I’ve ever tried to play with. Unintuitive and with a controller feels like a total afterthought. You are thrown into a few dozen loadout choices immediately and if you take time to read about your loot you’ll probably die. 

Maybe you can get used to it but the juice doesn’t feel worth the squeeze.

Marathon is not worth your time and money, it just isn't.

This is a game with effort and budget put into it, I can see where (some) of the reported $250mil budget went without a dobut. But its choice of aesthetic, well polished and intentional though it may be, is incredibly bland feeling in practice despite the vibrant colors. Habitat layouts and elements repeat and while there are of course unique "central feature" elements to each map, the rest is easy to get lost in visually as the samey-ness overwhelms your senses. 

Inventory management is unintuitive from both UI and UX perspectives and there's too much "garbage loot" (auto-sold on extract for money) relative to default (even a lightly expanded) in-round inventory. Spending the first hours of the game working out what's garbage, what looks like garbage but can provide rep, and what's needed for advancement is not skill expression. As a default part of the genre experience it serves to do nothing but slow new players down and make them easy-pickings. Other extraction-shooters streamline the "choice paralysis" phase, balancing the loot pool so that there's more "truly useful" than "half-garbage" laying about. Bungie seems to think that garbage-loot's secondary role is providing lore and to that end there's garbage everywhere. The game is also bad about identifying what mods go with which weapons or highlighting which slot the body-mod you just equipped went into. Inventory items (especially in-game consumables like bullets and meds) have low stack sizes for an extraction shooter as well; I understand the balance/gameplay-tension Bungie wanted here but the end result is more annoying that strategic.

Returning to UI/UX, the format and experience is so poor that there's a "help I don't understand anything on this page" button for every screen. Take that in for a second. Overall a decent mid tier game, but just not enough to keep a player base active enough and engaged for a long stretch of time, when there’s already so many pre-established extraction shooters with a far more dedicated community.

I’d give Marathon a 4/10, and perhaps a high 6/10 at the most for certain game and gun play moments that piqued my interest at the time, but quickly faded afterwards.

claims.claim: The game lacks Linux support due to anti-cheat restrictions with BattlEye.

citations.review_text:
I'd be glad to play the game, it looks really nice, however regardless of the Linux support thread on the feedback Discord being the biggest one there, they still haven't enabled Linux support in BattlEye (which DOES support Linux).

I am really disappointed, as letting Linux players in could actually bring up the player numbers... especially in the game's current state.

Bungie is ignoring a player base over a SINGLE TOGGLE SWITCH ON BATTLEYE. Battleye is fully supported on proton/linux but they refuse to enable it. If this is supposed to be Bungie's big comeback locking out an entire Linux desktop and Steam deck community is a massive error here. You're leaving money and a player count on the table for zero technical reason. This is a policy issue not a platform port issue. And yes I waited in the main menu to even post this ridiculous review of unsupported OS in 2026. I did watch my friend play it the game looks really fun.

I played the game for a little bit and liked it, but I recently moved to Linux as my main OS and can no longer play the game due to anti-cheat restrictions. I reserve my Windows partition for work.

Please enable Linux support for BattlEye. Steam has a BattlEye client for Proton that other games support. This would also let people play Marathon on the Steam Deck and Steam Machine.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features high-quality gunplay, strong sound design, and a unique art style.

citations.review_text:
I honestly wanted to recommend this game, I really do, but as someone who played other extraction shooters, I just don't know who this game is really for... The matchmaking is completly imbalanced, veteran players allow new players zero chance to grow and the addition of the PVE mode made that even worst as most casuals just play that, turning the PvP parts of the game into a rough grind between the sweatiest players in the game. Loot still feels meh and with no realy sense of reward. (You're better off fighting other people for their equipment than just normal looting) Progression is extremly overlwhelming from the start; so many systems that you need to keep track of and on top of all of that, you are forced into a wipe system that takes it all away, which wouldn't have been such a bad thing if it wasn't for the amount of progress you actually lose...

The worldsetting of the game is very unique and close to none and the visual asethetic is bar none. The gun play is very solid and the AI is actually rather challenging. It's just that the game really feels unrewarding for the amount of time you put in this game and unless you're someone who really likes the combat and gameplay loop, there's really hardly any redeeming qualities here.

To top it all off, the main build almost every veteran player uses in this game is an invisibility + wallhack build, forcing your to either use the same on your team or at the very least use thermal scopes and goodluck playing this game without friends unless you're a top player. If you're a casual or a destiny fan? Just steer away, this game is unfortunately not for you.

Marathon is an interesting topic.

The artstyle is great, it's unique, it's interesting.
Yet it seems halfway through development they decided to ditch any common sense and make guns look like someone's first attempt at modeling a sci-fi mug in blender, unfortunately, as much as they hoped for it to do so, the artstyle didn't manage to cover it up.

The gunplay has a nice kick to it: it feels like your guns actually pack a punch, something bungie games are known for.
You know what else bungie games used to be known for? bullet sponges.
Marathon carried that curse.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the game requires an always-online connection and lacks an offline mode.

citations.review_text:
So I've given this time to sit after I played it and refunded it. I wanted to give my thoughts on the game, for as limited as my time with it was.

The sound design, UI, visuals & art direction, even the story, limited as it is, are all incredible. Bungie hit it out of the park, and, in any other genre with more of a bent towards narrative, this game would be one of a rare few; a sequel coming decades after the series ended that faithfully followed in the footsteps of its predecessor and matched it for quality.

The problem, inherently, is the multiplayer-only nature of the gameplay. This game could remain a roguelike in its basic design, but making this game a live-service, always-online multiplayer-exclusive extraction shooter hinders it in fundamental ways that will lead to the hard work of the developers being canned by a parent company that cannot afford to let Bungie keep the lights on. If this game was made fully offline, with the option (not the requirement) to play in squads of your friends against NPC runners, then I would buy this game again at full price because everything else about this game deserves to be experienced. 

I fear, however, that asking that is effectively asking Bungie to have made a different game. This isn't the Marathon I wanted. It is, unfortunately, the one I got.

Don't get me wrong. The game is fun. Very fun even. But it's not gonna hold up as online only. As sad as it is I was hopeful that it would find it's niche and just be like that. I mean even 10k players would be ok for an extraction shooter. But 2k players and droping? That's no good. If they won't add an offline mode the game will die in the near future and that would be it. In such a case my money will be simply wasted on this game. And that's going to everyone who bought it.

The gunplay feels good, very reminiscent of Destiny; Some of the artwork within loading screens and cutscenes is genuinely really good(Albeit uncontextual and basically has nothing to with the actual game.), and the soundtrack can be phenomenal at times, but I think that's about where the good ends. 

The game feels directionless, very reminiscent of Arc Raiders; An extraction shooter with no goal other than to extract with unfathomable amounts of borderline useless loot(Minus weapons, of which you use to gain more useless loot.). I don't fully blame the game for it though, I think it's a genre problem & an oversaturation problem. 

Give the game more direction and actual reason to log in and raid, without just selling you bundles of actually awful skins for £25, and shoddy battlepasses; Then the game might actually be more successful, other than that it's just another PvPvE extraction shooter to collect dust on the shelf of the same stuff that came before it. 

4 out of 10, for me.

I really did try to make this game work for me, but this specific thing leaves a bitter aftertaste in my mouth. 

Since when a 40$ game can have a PAID battlepass and PAID cosmetics and everyone thinks it's okay? I have no words for that. I understand that Bungie had to make ends meet, but it just feels like a cashgrab atp. I am very dissapointed. 

On another note, I do not enjoy the UI at all. I've seen some people praise it. While I see the overall appeal and how people think it is beautiful, it is just NOT practical at all. It is difficult to read, and just not easy to use. I sometimes get too confused at what I am looking at. 

I think removing the BP and improving the UI would make this game better. 
Overall, if you don't mind this game being greedy and having a janky UI, you can give it a try.

I ABSOLUTELY DO NOT Like extraction shooters but this game is TOP NOTCH.

Gunplay is great. Story is fun to learn about. It is unique to itself as far as art style. I love what they have and I hope they release a battle royale at some point so less sweaty people can just enjoy the game from a competitive standpoint and less of a grindy grind. 

The game receives far too much unwarranted hate and half the time its going to be from people who have yet to even TRY it for themselves. Try the game please.

"The greatest game that some people may never play" - There is something incredibly special about this game. I wasn't someone who was sure I'd enjoy Marathon, but its the first time in a long time that I've been so addicted to a game, and I genuinely was shocked when I looked at my time played and saw I had surpassed 300 hours. The gunplay feels like what you'd expect from Bungie classics like Halo and Destiny, and every encounter with a hostile team feels like an adrenaline rush. It feels like a love letter to all of the classics, with certain weapons even feeling like callbacks to some all time greats. Outside of combat, every run has the potential to give you super high highs and can also give you super low lows, but as you continue to play the game it rewards you for your time spent through the faction system that makes it easier to recover more after losses. The style and aesthetic is so deeply thought out, it feels like such a unique world with its own rules and lore that will suck you in as you discover more. The style has grown on me so much the more I've engaged with the world. The game isn't without flaws, and it has had ups and downs obviously, but Bungie has been pretty quick to address hot button issues and I truly hope that the game finds its footing because its quickly become my new favorite game. It can be brutal and hard to approach at first, but as you play more, play with friends, and start to master the gameplay loop and combat, it feels so rewarding and so fun to chase that next big score.

It's a Bungie game.  

The weapons feel great.  The aesthetics are familiar and alien at the same time.  The sound design is incredible.  The gameplay is fast paced and intense.  There have been questionable design choices and development decisions, but in a way that reminds me of old school Bungie: they've been up front about what they're doing, why, and what they hope to accomplish.  They almost never implement something with the mindset of "this is how it's going to be" but rather one of "we're going to try this and you guys let us know how it feels".  This is extremely rare in modern AAA development teams and something I wish more people gave them credit for.  

In that vein, don't let the negativity you see push you away from trying out the game if you feel like you would enjoy it, but don't force yourself to play an extraction shooter if you already know you don't enjoy them.

This review is a token of respect and encouragement for this game and team.
Marathon is not perfect -not close- but how many games can boast of such an achievement?
Despite everything you might hear outside or within the Marathon community, I urge you to keep an open mind and save some room on your shelf for this game.

At the time of review, Ive played nearly 350h. 
From day 1 to today, its been 6 months since release.

[h2]VISUALS :[/h2]
Marathon is a game with a peculiar esthetic, quite unique, especially in gaming. 
It can feel a bit unorthodox for anyone not accustomed with experimental or hyper stylized visuals.
Some hate it the moment they look at it, some love it, and some remain open to being swayed.

A big part of the respect I have for that game, is for it to be looking the way it is. 
In this current era, safe realistic and generic stylized games are often favored as their predecessors paved the way for most. 
Within the AAA industry, this artstyle isnt just a choice, its a statement, and the same way Sea of Thieves and Fornite are reference points on their own, so is now Marathon.
It is not an easy feat, and you can clearly feel playing the game that the art team poured a lot in making the visuals a unique and recognizable experience.

Yet it can feel repulsive for some, please spend some time in the world, immerse yourself and keep your mind open. In a world where everything goes so fast, its not so bad to take your time falling in love with something.

[h2]GAMEPLAY: [/h2]
Gunplay here is not a concern. Most reviews will mention: its clearly one of the highlights of that game.
Every gun has its own specificities and animations. From the overheating mechanic for some, to the reloading, railgun system, etc ...
Shooting feels good, killing feels great.

The Shells (the class you choose) a…

Marathon wasn’t even on my radar at first. I decided to give it a shot during the free weekend, and I was immediately hooked. The gunplay feels incredible, the visual art style is fantastic, the sound design is immersive, and the different maps each bring something unique to the experience.

The thing about this game is that it gets immensely better the more time you put into it. I’m closing in on 200 hours, and I’m still discovering things about the game that I had no idea existed. There’s a surprising amount of depth here, and the more you learn, the more rewarding the game becomes.

I completely understand that extraction shooters aren’t for everyone, and yeah, things can get pretty sweaty at times. But I really appreciate how much the devs are listening to the community and actively working on improving the new-player experience. They’re even adding PvE options to accommodate players who aren’t interested in the PvP sweatiness.

I’ve bought this game for myself and two other friends, and I even convinced my brother to pick it up. We all absolutely love it.

Honestly, it saddens me to see this game getting so much hate because I genuinely don’t think it deserves it. Marathon is easily my Game of the Year so far. I really think people need to stop sleeping on this game. It has great bones, an incredible foundation, and so much potential to become something even better as new content continues to roll out.

For me, this is a 10/10. If you’ve been on the fence, give it a real shot and put some time into it. You might be surprised by how much there is to love.

After one full season of 3 months, here is a short review of Marathon.

Short premise that i have about 2000 hours in Hunt Showdown, 300 hours in Arc Raiders and i have also played Tarkov, The Cycle and some other less noteworthy games in this exact genre to compare Marathon to.

The worldbuilding, gunplay, atmosphere and sounddesign are exceptionally good. 
Nothing compares to naything i have ever played in terms of extracitonshooters. A lot of Games aim for super realistic settings and a scenario that could actually be true in a parallel timeline or universe. 
Marathon aims for something unique and expresses it with shapes and forms, colors and sounds, feel and impact. This exactly is what makes Marathon stand out of the rest of its genre-colleagues: It is a Game that actually feels and looks like a game, which is a nice change and something people may have not felt in a very long time.

The Systems in Season 1 were a good foundation but needed some work in terms of progressionpacing explanation and balancing, which they will iron out in season 2. 
Doing contracts, interacting with the world and its system was fun and fresh, even though the onboarding and explanaiton was a little bit rough at first but once it clicks, you wil have no problem navigating, understanding and using the systems given to you.
Its also important to me to mention that Marathon is very generous with loot, rewards and everything else that you need to stay afloat in the game. Marathons surface seems too hardcore for people watchign the game but when you get into it and stay focussed on progress and actually doing objectives, you will not only have a lot of fun stuff to do but you will also ramp up gear, experience and knowledge while having a challenge that is still fun.

The Runnershells are unique in their appearance, playstyle and abilities, which makes the current roster open for every playstyle you can possibly want. It does not matter if you want to play aggressive, supportive, defensiv…

This is a long read.
